Captured PDF (extracted text):

ECEN 248 — Introduction to Digital Systems Design
Texas A&M University, Fall 2026

Instructor: Dr. Pradeep Kashinath
Office: ZACH 425 (Zachry Engineering Education Complex)
Email: kashinath@tamu.edu
Office Hours: T/R 2:00–3:30 PM, or by appointment

Meeting Times
- Lecture: MWF 11:30 AM – 12:20 PM, ZACH 350
- Lab: T 1:50–4:40 PM or W 2:00–4:50 PM (sections vary by registration)

Textbook (Required)
Fundamentals of Logic Design, 7th ed., Roth & Kinney. Either physical or electronic copy is fine.

Course Description
Fundamentals of digital systems design: Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential logic circuits, finite state machines, and basic computer organization. Students design and verify digital circuits using SystemVerilog on Basys 3 FPGA development boards. The course is a prerequisite for ECEN 350 (Computer Architecture) and ECEN 449 (Microprocessor System Design).

Learning Outcomes
By the end of the course you should be able to:
1. Apply Boolean algebra and Karnaugh maps to simplify logic expressions.
2. Design combinational circuits using basic gates, multiplexers, and decoders.
3. Design synchronous sequential circuits using flip-flops and finite state machines.
4. Write synthesizable SystemVerilog and verify behavior on an FPGA.
5. Reason about timing, propagation delay, and basic computer organization.

Grading Breakdown
- Homework (6 assignments): 20%
- Lab assignments (10): 25%
- Midterm Exam: 20%
- Final Exam: 25%
- Weekly quizzes (lowest 2 dropped): 10%

Letter grade thresholds: A ≥ 90, B ≥ 80, C ≥ 70, D ≥ 60, F < 60. No curve unless class average falls below 70.

Schedule — Key Dates
- HW 1 due: Fri Sep 11, 2026 (11:59 PM via Canvas)
- HW 2 due: Fri Sep 25, 2026
- Midterm Exam: Wed Oct 14, 2026, in class, ZACH 350
- HW 3 due: Fri Oct 23, 2026
- HW 4 due: Fri Nov 6, 2026
- Project Proposal due: Mon Nov 9, 2026
- HW 5 due: Fri Nov 20, 2026
- Thanksgiving holiday: Nov 25–27 (no class, no lab)
- Final Project Demo: Fri Dec 4, 2026 (during your registered lab section)
- HW 6 due: Fri Dec 4, 2026
- Final Exam: Tue Dec 15, 2026, 3:30–5:30 PM, ZACH 350

Lab Policy
Labs are completed individually in the FPGA lab. Pre-lab exercises are due 24 hours before your lab section starts. Bring your Basys 3 board and laptop to every lab. Lab attendance is required; one missed lab can be made up by attending another section the same week with prior approval from your TA.

Late Work
Homework: 20% penalty per calendar day, max 3 days late. No credit after that. Lab pre-labs cannot be turned in late. Project deliverables (proposal, demo) cannot be turned in late without a documented excuse.

Academic Integrity
All submitted work must be your own. Discussing concepts is fine; sharing code, solutions, or screenshots is not. Violations will be reported to the Aggie Honor Council. The honor code is a single sentence: "An Aggie does not lie, cheat, or steal, or tolerate those who do."

Accommodations
Students requiring accommodations should contact Disability Resources (DR) within the first two weeks of the semester. Submit your DR letter to the instructor as early as possible — accommodations cannot be applied retroactively.

Required Materials
- Basys 3 FPGA development board (campus bookstore, approx. $165)
- Vivado WebPACK (free from Xilinx/AMD, install on personal laptop)
- Pen/pencil for the lab notebook (provided)

Communication
- Course questions: post on Piazza (link on Canvas). Other students may answer faster than the instructor.
- Grading or personal issues: email the instructor or your TA directly.
- Response time: ~24 hours on weekdays, ~48 hours on weekends.

Tentative Topic Schedule
Week 1: Number systems, binary arithmetic
Week 2: Boolean algebra, gate-level logic
Week 3–4: Combinational design, K-maps, hazards
Week 5: Multiplexers, decoders, arithmetic circuits
Week 6: Latches and flip-flops
Week 7: Midterm review and exam
Week 8: Synchronous sequential circuits
Week 9–10: Finite state machine design
Week 11: Memory, register files, SystemVerilog
Week 12: Datapath and control unit design
Week 13: Project work
Week 14: Final project demos, final review
Finals week
